concept.body: Two geometric-mean relationships in the altitude picture. ALTITUDE = geometric mean of the two hypotenuse SEGMENTS: h = √(p·q). LEG = geometric mean of the whole HYPOTENUSE and the segment adjacent to that leg: leg = √(hyp·adj). Geometric mean of a and b is always √(ab) — square root of the product, not the average.

explanationVariants: Geometric mean of a and b is √(ab): for 9 and 16 that's √144 = 12.

widget.prompt: What is the geometric mean of 9 and 16?

commonErrors.feedback: 12.5 = (9 + 16)/2 is the average. Geometric mean is √(9 × 16) = 12.
144 = 9 × 16 is the product. Take its square root: √144 = 12.

steps.body: The **geometric mean** of two numbers a and b is √(ab) — the value x where a/x = x/b. It's the 'multiplicative middle,' the way the average is the additive middle. In the altitude picture, the equal ratios between similar triangles turn directly into geometric means.

widget.prompt: What is the geometric mean of 4 and 9? (√(4 × 9))

commonErrors.feedback: 6.5 = (4 + 9)/2 is the ARITHMETIC mean (average). The GEOMETRIC mean is √(4 × 9) = √36 = 6.
36 = 4 × 9 is the product itself. The geometric mean takes its SQUARE ROOT: √36 = 6.

explanationVariants: The altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments: h = √(p·q).
From the similar triangles, p/h = h/q, so h² = pq and h = √(pq).

widget.prompt: The altitude h to the hypotenuse relates to the two hypotenuse segments p and q how?

options.label: h = √(p·q) — the geometric mean of the segments
options.feedback: The similar triangles give p/h = h/q, so h² = pq and h is the geometric mean √(pq).

options.label: h = (p + q)/2 — the average
options.feedback: That's the ARITHMETIC mean. The altitude is the GEOMETRIC mean: h = √(pq).

options.label: h = p + q — the whole hypotenuse
options.feedback: p + q is the full hypotenuse length, not the altitude. The altitude is √(pq).

options.label: h = p·q — the product
options.feedback: The product is under a square root: h = √(pq), not pq itself.

widget.prompt: The hypotenuse is 25. Slide the foot until it splits into 9 and 16, and read the altitude — then keep sliding and check whether h² = p·q was a fact about those two numbers or about every position.
widget.successFeedback: 9 and 16, and the altitude reads 12 — because 12² = 144 = 9 × 16. That is what "geometric mean" names: h is the number whose square is the product of the two segments. Every other position you passed through obeyed it too, which is why it is a theorem and not a coincidence about 9 and 16.
widget.lowFeedback: p is still under 9, so the left segment is too short and the altitude is shorter than 12. Slide right — h grows while p is the smaller segment, then shrinks again once p overtakes q.
widget.highFeedback: p has gone past 9. Ease back left. Watch the altitude as you do: it peaks at the midpoint, where p and q are equal, and falls away toward both ends.

predict.prompt: The altitude to a hypotenuse splits it into 9 and 16. The altitude's length will be…

options.label: 12.5 — the average of 9 and 16 is close enough

predict.reveal: 12, and the route is the product rather than the sum: √(9 × 16) = √144. Half the hypotenuse is 12.5, which is close enough to 12 to hide the mistake here and to fail badly on any less balanced split — at 4 and 21 the mean is 12.5 and the altitude is only about 9.2.

steps.body: Each **leg** is a geometric mean too — of the whole hypotenuse and the segment ADJACENT to that leg: leg = √(hypotenuse × adjacent segment). Two flavors: the altitude is the geometric mean of the two SEGMENTS; a leg is the geometric mean of the HYPOTENUSE and its adjacent segment. Keep them straight.

widget.prompt: A right triangle's hypotenuse is 25, split by the altitude into 9 and 16. The leg adjacent to the segment of 9 has length √(25 × 9). What is that leg?

commonErrors.feedback: 34 = 25 + 9 adds. The leg is the geometric mean √(25 × 9) = 15.

explanationVariants: A leg is the geometric mean of the WHOLE hypotenuse and its adjacent segment; the altitude is the geometric mean of the two SEGMENTS.

widget.prompt: To find a LEG using the geometric mean, you take the square root of…

options.label: The hypotenuse times its adjacent segment
options.feedback: leg = √(hypotenuse × adjacent segment) — the leg is the geometric mean of the whole and its near segment.

options.label: The two hypotenuse segments multiplied
options.feedback: That gives the ALTITUDE, not a leg. A leg uses the whole hypotenuse × its adjacent segment.

options.label: The two leg lengths multiplied together
options.feedback: The legs aren't multiplied together here. A leg = √(hypotenuse × adjacent segment).

options.label: The altitude times the full hypotenuse
options.feedback: That isn't one of the geometric-mean relationships. Use √(hypotenuse × adjacent segment) for a leg.

hints: The altitude is the geometric mean: h = √(p·q), so h² = p·q.
With h = 6 and one segment p = 4, solve 6² = 4·q.
explanationVariants: Since h² = p·q, we have 36 = 4·q, so q = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

widget.prompt: The altitude to a hypotenuse is 6, and one segment of the hypotenuse is 4. What is the OTHER segment?

takeaways: Geometric mean of a, b is √(ab) — where a/x = x/b.
Altitude = geometric mean of the two hypotenuse segments: h = √(p·q).
Leg = geometric mean of the whole hypotenuse and its adjacent segment: √(hyp × adj).
steps.teaser: Next: use these relationships to solve right triangles quickly.
